findings.description: The new symlink check in recordWindowSocket runs after the fix-round relaunch (relaunchWorker → writeSessionProfile) and first launch have already written compiled/ files, hook scripts included, through the same session dir. On those paths a symlinked session dir is followed before the guard throws; only respawn is protected. Sessions share the operator's uid (ADR 0106), so this is inconsistent hardening, not a new exploit.

ADR 0115 still says the protected check "tests a path in the glob's first segment"; this PR replaces that with an overlap check against protected entries at any depth, so the ADR (which wins over the design docs) now describes the old behavior.
`beneath` has one caller and hand-rebuilds what `reach(`${own.path}/`)` already returns for a trailing-`/` glob; rescopeReach could use that and drop `beneath`.
The JSDoc "The gate's protected paths." on `PROTECTED` only restates the constant's name and its PROTECTED_PATH_GLOBS source; delete it.

process_issues.description: Skipped review-context (no spec/protocol/infra surface), review-workflow-safety (no workflow change), review-maintainability (off default roster), review-spec (no closing issue or spec source).

Correctness's single important (symlink guard runs after earlier compiled-profile writes) was confirmed by its validator but downgraded to nit: no reachable harm under ADR 0106's same-uid model. Its respawn evidence was also partly wrong.
